title: CVE-2025-14524: bearer token leak on cross-protocol redirect
excerpt:
## Summary:
A vulnerability exists in `libcurl` regarding the handling of OAuth2 Bearer tokens (`CURLOPT_XOAUTH2_BEARER`) during HTTP redirects.

While `libcurl` correctly clears standard authentication credentials (`CURLOPT_USERPWD`) when following a redirect to a different host, port, or protocol (a security hardening introduced to fix CVE-2022-27774), it fails to apply the same logic to the OAuth2 Bearer token.

If an application using `libcurl` connects to a trusted server but is redirected to a malicious server (e.g., via an Open Redirect vulnerability) on a protocol supporting SASL (like IMAP, SMTP, or POP3), the valid Bearer token is automatically sent to the attacker. This happens because the token remains in the handle and is reused for the new connection, allowing the attacker to steal the credentials.

**AI Statement:** This report was researched and generated with the assistance of an AI agent to analyze the `libcurl` source code and identify inconsistent state management logic. However, the vulnerability has been manually verified, the Proof of Concept code was compiled and executed locally, and the findings have been confirmed against a custom TCP server to ensure validity and reproducibility.

## Affected version
The vulnerability was reproduced on the following version:

```text
curl 8.5.0 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/8.5.0 OpenSSL/3.0.13 zlib/1.3 brotli/1.1.0 zstd/1.5.5 libidn2/2.3.7 libpsl/0.21.2 (+libidn2/2.3.7) libssh/0.10.6/openssl/zlib nghttp2/1.59.0 librtmp/2.3 OpenLDAP/2.6.7
Release-Date: 2023-12-06, security patched: 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.6
Protocols: dict file ftp ftps gopher gophers http https imap imaps ldap ldaps mqtt pop3 pop3s rtmp rtsp scp sftp smb smbs smtp smtps telnet tftp
Features: alt-svc AsynchDNS brotli GSS-API HSTS HTTP2 HTTPS-proxy IDN IPv6 Kerberos Largefile libz NTLM PSL SPNEGO SSL threadsafe TLS-SRP UnixSockets zstd
```

## Vulnerable Code Analysis

The issue lies in the HTTP redirect handling logic (typically within `lib/http.c`, function `Curl_http_follow` or similar transfer logic depending on the version).

When `libcurl` detects a redirect that crosses a security boundary (change of host, port, or protocol), it explicitly clears the username and password to prevent leaks. However, it overlooks the Bearer token string.

summary: libcurl fails to clear OAuth2 Bearer tokens during cross-protocol redirects, allowing token leakage to attacker-controlled servers.

claims.text: OAuth2 Bearer token is not cleared when clearing standard credentials during redirects
claims.reasoning: The redirect handling code in Curl_http_follow explicitly clears user and password when redirecting to a different port or scheme (protocol), but there is no corresponding clear for the OAuth2 Bearer token. The Bearer token persists in the handle and is reused on the new connection.

citations.note: When clear=TRUE, only data->state.aptr.user and data->state.aptr.passwd are freed (lines 1345-1346). No clearing of data->set.str[STRING_BEARER] or equivalent Bearer token storage.
The 'Clear auth' block (lines 1298-1348) detects cross-port/protocol redirects but only clears user/password credentials.

claims.reasoning: The vulnerable logic is in lib/http.c in the Curl_http_follow function, specifically the 'Clear auth' block starting at line 1298.

citations.note: Curl_http_follow function definition at line 1206 contains the redirect handling logic including the credential clearing block at lines 1298-1348.

claims.text: redirect to a different protocol that supports SASL (e.g., IMAP)
claims.reasoning: The code detects protocol changes via scheme handler comparison (line 1337). The PoC demonstrates a cross-protocol redirect from HTTP to IMAP, which triggers the credential clearing logic but leaves the Bearer token intact.

citations.note: The code compares p->protocol != data->info.conn_protocol at line 1337 (master) / 1337 (release) to detect protocol/scheme changes, which would trigger clear=TRUE for IMAP, SMTP, POP3, etc.
PoC demonstrates HTTP->IMAP redirect with Location: imap://victim@127.0.0.1:1430/ triggering SASL AUTHENTICATE XOAUTH2.

claims.text: Bearer token is sent to attacker-controlled server, enabling credential theft
claims.reasoning: The PoC demonstrates successful exfiltration of the Bearer token to an attacker-controlled IMAP server. The token persists because it is not cleared during the cross-protocol redirect.

citations.note: PoC output shows '[!!!] STOLEN TOKEN: dXNlcj12aWN0aW0BYXV0aD1CZWFyZXIgTVlfU0VDUkVUX0dPTERFTl9USUNLRVQBAQ==' which decodes to the Bearer token.
Because the Bearer token is not cleared at lines 1345-1346, it remains in the handle and is sent to the new protocol endpoint.

claims.text: Use rogue_server.py to redirect HTTP request to imap://victim@127.0.0.1:1430/ and capture token via AUTHENTICATE XOAUTH2
claims.reasoning: The reproduction steps are concrete and the provided PoC code and server script demonstrate the vulnerability end-to-end.

citations.note: The rogue_server.py implements the exact reproduction: HTTP redirector on port 8080 sends 301 redirect to imap://victim@127.0.0.1:1430/, IMAP stealer on port 1430 captures token via AUTHENTICATE XOAUTH2.
The client sets CURLOPT_XOAUTH2_BEARER, CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION, CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS_STR="http,https,imap" and does NOT set CURLOPT_UNRESTRICTED_AUTH.

key_reasons: The Curl_http_follow function in lib/http.c (lines 1298-1348) clears user/password on cross-port/protocol redirects but omits clearing the OAuth2 Bearer token.
The deterministic checks confirm CURLOPT_XOAUTH2_BEARER exists and the code is grounded at the reported revision.
The PoC demonstrates a working exploit: HTTP->IMAP redirect leaks the Bearer token via SASL AUTHENTICATE XOAUTH2.
This is a regression/incomplete fix of CVE-2022-27774 which only addressed user/password credentials.
No project policy section classifies this as a non-security issue; it is a credential leakage across trust boundaries.
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and reproducible PoC. The code in lib/http.c (Curl_http_follow, lines 1298-1348) confirms the Bearer token is not cleared when user/password are cleared during cross-protocol redirects. This is a valid security issue — an incomplete fix for CVE-2022-27774. We will prepare a patch to clear the Bearer token alongside the other credentials.
